topics.name: Prepositions of place, time and movement
Phrases with prepositions (fond of, afraid of, in search of)

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct preposition.
options: The hole is far away of the tree.
The hole is far away to the tree.
The hole is far away from the tree.
questions.rule: We say far away from a place.

options: Bhaskaracharya wrote a famous book on arithmetic.
Bhaskaracharya writed a famous book on arithmetic.
Bhaskaracharya written a famous book on arithmetic.
questions.rule: Write is irregular: write - wrote - written. The simple past is wrote.

options: Leelavati was fond of lotus flowers.
Leelavati was fond with lotus flowers.
Leelavati was fond for lotus flowers.
questions.rule: The fixed phrase is fond of: to be fond of something.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Fly is irregular: fly - flew - flown. 'Flied' is not used.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use in with centuries, years and months: in the 5th century.

questions.after: do you go to school, by bus or on foot?
questions.rule: How asks about the way or means: by bus, by train, on foot.
The fixed phrase is afraid of.
Wh- question order: How far + is + subject: How far is the station?

chat: Did you see the peacock in the garden?
options: Yes, I seen it on the coconut tree.
Yes, I did saw it on the coconut tree.
Yes, I saw it on the coconut tree.
questions.rule: In a statement, the simple past of see is saw. After 'did', use the base form, so 'did saw' is wrong.

chat: I'm coming to Mumbai by train tomorrow!
options: Great! What time your train arrives?
Great! What time does your train arrives?
Great! What time does your train arrive?
questions.rule: Wh- question: What time + does + subject + base verb: does your train arrive?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The lotus were swaying in the wind.
The lotus was swaying in the wind.
The lotus was sway in the wind.
questions.rule: Past continuous = was/were + -ing. One lotus, so was swaying.

options: How much the train ticket costs?
How much does the train ticket cost?
How much does the train ticket costs?
questions.rule: Use does + base verb in the question: How much does it cost?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The fixed phrase is fond of, never 'fond on'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: were + -ing makes the past continuous, like chattering: were playing.

questions.before: The peacock saw a serpent moving
questions.rule: To shows movement towards a place: moving to its hole.

questions.after: the serpent just before it entered the hole.
questions.rule: Catch is irregular: catch - caught - caught.
Pattern: subject + is afraid of + noun.
Subject + past verb + object: Leelavati loved the graceful swan.

chat: I'm going to the science museum on Sunday.
questions.rule: Question order: How + will + you + base verb: How will you get there?

chat: What were you doing at five o'clock?
questions.rule: I takes was, and the past continuous needs -ing: I was solving.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct prepositions.
options: The train leaves at 8.45 am on Monday.
The train leaves in 8.45 am on Monday.
The train leaves at 8.45 am in Monday.
questions.rule: Use at with clock times and on with days: at 8.45 am on Monday.

options: The children was afraid of the large serpent.
The children were afraid from the large serpent.
The children were afraid of the large serpent.
questions.rule: Children is plural, so were; and the phrase is afraid of.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, the main verb is in its base form: does ... arrive.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: was + -ing makes the past continuous, like watching: was sitting.

questions.after: does a ticket to Mumbai cost?
questions.rule: Ask about price with How much ... cost?
The fixed phrase is proud of.
Past continuous: subject + were + -ing + place: were swimming.
Towards shows the direction of movement: flew straight towards its nest.
Did asks for the past (lived), and centuries take in.

chat: You can reach my house from the station by taxi.
options: How long the taxi ride takes?
How long does the taxi ride take?
How long does the taxi ride took?
questions.rule: Wh- question: How long + does + subject + base verb: does it take?

options: 'Leelavati' was a book that taught arithmetic through verses.
'Leelavati' were a book that taught arithmetic through verses.
'Leelavati' was a book that teached arithmetic through verses.
questions.rule: One book takes was; teach is irregular: teach - taught.

options: The peacock was sitting on the tree when it saw the serpent.
The peacock sitting on the tree when it saw the serpent.
The peacock was sitting on the tree when it was see the serpent.
questions.rule: Longer action: was sitting; sudden short action: simple past saw.

options: Ravi walked across of the bridge and into the temple.
Ravi walked across the bridge and into the temple.
Ravi walk across the bridge and into the temple.
questions.rule: Across needs no 'of', and a finished past action takes the past: walked.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The fixed phrase is afraid of, even with 'never' in between.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Kiran is singular, so the helper is does: Where does Kiran live?

questions.after: about Aryabhata when the bell rang.
questions.rule: An action in progress when another happened: were reading (we takes were).
Use for with a length of time (hundreds of years); since needs a starting point.
Wh- question: When + does + subject + base verb.

chat: Why do you visit the library so often?
options: Because I am fond to reading about Indian mathematicians.
Because I am fond of reading about Indian mathematicians.
Because I fond of reading about Indian mathematicians.
questions.rule: Fond of + -ing; and the sentence needs the verb am.

chat: What did you learn in your maths class today?
options: We learnt how to find square roots.
We learnt how to found square roots.
We learnt how to finding square roots.
questions.rule: After how to, use the base verb: how to find.

options: The peacock flew down from the branch and swooped upon the serpent.
The peacock flew down of the branch and swooped upon the serpent.
The peacock flew down from the branch and swooped upon to the serpent.
questions.rule: Movement away from a place uses from; upon already means 'on', so no 'to'.

options: Do you know what time does the train leave?
Do you know what time the train leave?
Do you know what time the train leaves?
questions.rule: Inside a bigger question, the wh- part uses statement order: what time the train leaves.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Long ago and wrote show the past, so the joined verb is past too: explained.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The sudden action that interrupts takes the simple past: a peacock suddenly flew past.

questions.before: The farmer went to the market
questions.rule: The fixed phrase is in search of + noun: looking for something.

questions.after: of the two books on Indian mathematics did you like more?
questions.rule: Use Which to choose from a small, known group: which of the two books.
Past continuous question: What + were + you + -ing?
Fond of is followed by a noun or an -ing word: fond of walking.

chat: How do I get to your house from the station?
options: Take a taxi from the station till my house.
Take a taxi from the station to my house.
Take a taxi from the station in my house.
questions.rule: For a journey, use from ... to. 'Till' is for time, not places.

chat: I went to Mumbai last weekend. Ask me anything!
questions.rule: Past question: did + subject + base verb: How did you travel?
